incident-bot: Pager: SEV-1 — deploy canary failing (v2026.03.15-canary). Error spike on hosted API (model requests 500/503). Paging oncall @Ryan. See alerts: https://alerts.redwood.ai/SEV-1/1794001234 :rotating_light:
Maya: Ack. Ryan — taking. Quick summary pls.
Thomas: Canary rollout started 00:12 UTC. After ~3 minutes canary instances started returning 500s. Error logs show KMS decrypt failures for the model key, and feature-flagged traffic is hitting the new route.
Jen: I pulled logs from canary pods: `AccessDeniedException: Request had insufficient authentication scopes. com.google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService/Decrypt denied to serviceAccount:svc-redwood@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com` Also noticed env `KMS_KEY_ID` set to `projects/prod/locations/global/keyRings/models/cryptoKeys/model-key-v2` — that key was rotated an hour ago.
Alex: Release page: <https://deploys.redwood/releases/v2026.03.15-canary|v2026.03.15-canary>. Feature flag `model-v2-route` was enabled for 10% canary traffic at deploy. We have a kill-switch in Flags Console.
Ryan: ETA for rollback? Is toggling flag faster? Impact?
Liz: Support seeing customer 503s — about 12% of calls failing, spike to 18% at worst; multiple seats reported intermittent failures. No major data loss but SLOs breached for latency/error.
Thomas: Canary pods failing early during initialization when they attempt to decrypt model weights/keys at startup. So toggling feature flag might stop traffic routing to the new code path but won't fix background jobs that try to load keys.
Jen: Reproduction check: `kubectl -n inference logs deploy/api-canary --since=5m | grep Decrypt` shows repeated KMS errors. Quick mitigation options: 1) rollback canary, 2) flip feature flag kill-switch (reduces user-facing errors), 3) grant KMS permission to service account. Rollback is fastest to reduce customer impact.
Maya: If rollback reduces customer impact immediately that's preferred. Can we do both toggle-flag + rollback?
Alex: I can flip the flag now via console or API. Doing API so it's recorded: ```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  https://flags.redwood.ai/api/v1/flags/model-v2-route/toggle \
  -d '{"state":"off","actor":"alex"}'
```
Alex: flipped `model-v2-route` -> OFF :white_check_mark: Partial reduction in traffic to canary, error rate dropped from 18% -> ~7% in 30s but background jobs still showing KMS errors.
Jen: Background jobs (embeddings/async loaders) still failing as they try to decrypt with the new key at startup. Checking IAM: `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy projects/prod/locations/global/keyRings/models/cryptoKeys/model-key-v2 --format=json` shows no binding for `serviceAccount:svc-redwood@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com`. Looks like rotation updated key policy to be restrictive.
Jen: If we can add `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` to that service account for the new key, that should fix decrypts. Command: ```bash
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding projects/prod/locations/global/keyRings/models/cryptoKeys/model-key-v2 \
  --member="serviceAccount:svc-redwood@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
  --role="roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter"
```
Maya: Can someone run that? Any reason not to grant temporarily?
Thomas: It's low risk for short term; but safest is rollback while we update IAM and then redeploy. Rollback is simpler and avoids granting cross-key permissions quickly.
Ryan: I agree — rollback canary now, then apply IAM fix. Thomas can you trigger rollback and Jen follow-up with IAM change?
Thomas: Rolling back now. `redwood-deploy rollback --release v2026.03.14 --service api-gateway --env prod --target canary` -> started. deploy-bot: `deploy-bot: Rollback job 782 started by Thomas. ETA ~2m.`
deploy-bot: `Pods scaled down for v2026.03.15-canary; v2026.03.14 replicas restoring.`
Thomas: Rollback complete. Monitoring: error rate dropped from 7% -> 1.6% within 90s. Latency normalized.
Liz: Customer update: posting to status page now. Draft: "We experienced elevated errors due to a configuration issue introduced during deploy. The canary has been rolled back and services are recovering. We will follow up with root cause and timeline for permanent fix." Approving.
Jen: Running IAM grant now so we can redeploy safely: `gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding ...model-key-v2 --member="serviceAccount:svc-redwood@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com" --role="roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter"` -> applied. Verified via `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy` shows binding present.
Alex: After IAM fix I started a dry-run redeploy to canary in staging. Also added a pre-deploy gate to CI: check `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy` contains required binding for svc account or fail the job. Patch PR: https://git.redwood.ai/p/infra/+/2345
Maya: Good. Action items: 1) Jen — run IAM binding change in prod and document (owner Jen), 2) Thomas — add canary pre-check + block if KMS binding missing (owner Thomas), 3) Alex — add flag safety net to auto-fail deploys if background jobs hit KMS error on init (owner Alex), 4) Support to notify impacted customers with a postmortem (owner Liz).
Ryan: Oncall handoff — I'll stay for 45m to ride the deploy. If everything stable, I’ll update the incident channel and hand back to Maya.
Maya: Thanks team. Summary: root cause = key rotation produced a key with stricter IAM (missing service account binding) which the canary attempted to use; feature-flagged route amplified user visibility. Mitigation = flipped feature flag then rolled back canary; applied IAM binding; monitoring shows recovery.
incident-bot: Incident SEV-1 resolved by rollback and IAM fix. Creating incident ticket INC-2026-1794001234 and scheduling 1-hour postmortem at 2026-03-15T03:30:00Z.
Maya: Please add the deploy artifacts and logs to the ticket and link PRs.
Liz: I'll send the customer follow-up and attach timeline.
Thomas: Leaving a troubleshooting note: consider moving KMS binding checks into the operator that provisions keys + automation to sync service accounts during rotation.
Alex: Also recommend a small automation: if a canary sees `KMS Decrypt` errors > threshold during init, auto-stop rollout and revert traffic.
Maya: Closing thread for now. Great work — we triaged, mitigated, and have owners for follow-ups. :tada:
